title: Signer and Channel Matrix for Occupancy and Residency Certification Plans
content:
Who must sign the annual occupancy certification, how many distinct signatures complete a cycle, and which signing channels count differ from plan to plan within the Occupancy and Residency Certification product. The matrix below is the reference for every plan.

## Required signers and signature count

| Plan | Who must sign | Distinct signers needed to complete one cycle |
|---|---|---|
| Standard Annual Certification | the borrower | 1 |
| Joint Borrower Certification | each living borrower | 2 |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | each living borrower and the eligible non-borrowing spouse | 2 |
| Deferral Period Certification | the eligible non-borrowing spouse | 1 |
| Living Trust Certification | the trustee and each living borrower | 2 |
| Authorized Representative Certification | the attorney-in-fact or guardian | 1 |

Under every plan, a signer missing from a partial certification may supply the missing signature within 15 calendar days after the partial certification without a new request.

## Signing channels that count

| Plan | Recorded phone certification by the signer | Servicing-portal certification | Signed paper certification returned by mail |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Annual Certification | counts | counts | counts |
| Joint Borrower Certification | counts | counts | counts |
| Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification | counts | counts | counts |
| Deferral Period Certification | does not count | counts | counts |
| Living Trust Certification | does not count | does not count | counts |
| Authorized Representative Certification | does not count | counts | counts |

## Points of reading

- A mailed, signed paper certification counts under all six plans.
- The phone channel counts only under Standard Annual, Joint Borrower and Non-Borrowing Spouse Household Certification.
- Living Trust Certification is the only plan on which a servicing-portal certification does not count.
- The signature count is a count of *distinct* signers: two certifications from the same person are one signer.

**Hypothetical illustration.** On a Joint Borrower Certification profile, one living borrower certifies by phone and the other signs a paper form returned by mail: both channels count under that plan, and the two distinct signers meet the required count of 2. On a Living Trust Certification profile the same phone certification would not count, because only the mail channel counts under that plan.
